thread:
oncall-bot: PAGER: KV cache saturation detected in ntk-rope pool (hosts: ntk-rope-03/07/11). Cache size delta +420% over baseline, sustained >95% fill for 6m. High tail latency and continuous-batching failures observed. Incident ts=2333333333
Maya B: I'm on it. Seeing a correlated jump in prefetch queue depth and eviction rate. Prefetch spike started ~2333333200.
Sanjay K: Checking rollout logs — we pushed rope.long_context_prefetch=true at 2333332400 to 60% canary. That rollout aligns with the start window.
Ingrid L: Confirmed. Canary subset: ntk-rope-02/03/07. Those hosts show 3-4x more KV lookups per request.
Leo P: Likely interaction: sliding-window prefetch + continuous batching causing exponential KV footprints. Quick mitigation options: 1) disable long_context_prefetch feature-flag; 2) reduce batch_max_tokens; 3) set prefetch window to fixed small value.
Maya B: CS reports two customers seeing 500s in chat endpoints. @Customer Success can you paste the error snippets?
Customer Success: customer-a: "chat: upstream 500 internal server error - timeout writing to model"; customer-b: repeated partial responses + socket closes. Both correlated at 2333333300-2333333350.
Sanjay K: I'm going to apply a conservative hotpatch to yarn config to cap batch size and prefetch window on the canary hosts first. Running command now.
Sanjay K: ```kubectl -n ntk patch configmap rope-prefetch --patch '{"data":{"window":"64","max_batch_tokens":"256"}}'```
ops-runbot: ✅ patch applied to ntk-rope-02/03/07.
Maya B: Monitoring metrics. Eviction rate down ~30% in 90s. Latency tails still elevated but trending down.
Ingrid L: Good. Can we also flip the FF for long_context_prefetch back to off on the canary? If that reduces pressure we can roll full rollback.
Leo P: I'll toggle canary FF off. Doing safe toggle (canary only).
Leo P: ```curl -s -X POST https://ff.redwood.internal/toggle -d 'flag=rope.long_context_prefetch&state=off&target=canary' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN'```
ops-runbot: FF toggle succeeded (canary scope).
Maya B: After toggle: prefetch queue depth collapsed by 65% within 2m; KV cache growth flattened.
Sanjay K: Nice. I'm preparing a cluster-wide rollback plan if we want to revert full rollout. Proposed steps: 1) throttle continuous batching globally (batch_max_tokens -> 256), 2) set prefetch window fixed=64 for all rope pools, 3) rollback feature flag rollout to 0%.
Ingrid L: +1. Do we need a DB migration or any on-disk changes?
Sanjay K: No disk changes. Just config/FF toggles and an orchestration for canary -> global. Impact window should be minimal aside from slightly higher per-token cost due to smaller batches.
Maya B: CS, small heads up to affected customers with ETA ~15m for full mitigation if we rollout global rollback.
Customer Success: sending interim note, will request logs and follow up with SLA owners.
Maya B: OK executing global rollback now in controlled steps. Step 1: set batch_max_tokens to 256 for all rope pools.
Sanjay K: ```helm upgrade rope-runtime --set continuousBatch.maxTokens=256 --reuse-values --namespace=runtime || true```
ops-runbot: Helm jobs queued; patch rollout starting across 12 nodes (rolling update).
Maya B: Watching metrics: KV evictions peaked earlier, now trending to baseline. Tail latency P99 improved from 2.2s -> 0.9s on canary.
Ingrid L: Rolling prefetch window change next.
Sanjay K: ```kubectl -n ntk patch cm rope-prefetch -p '{"data":{"window":"64"}}' --selector=app=rope-runtime```
ops-runbot: Prefetch window rollout progressing; 6/12 nodes updated.
Maya B: After 10 min into global steps: overall cache delta baseline +12% (acceptable). No new 500 reports from customers.
Customer Success: Customers acknowledged mitigation, will keep monitoring and escalate if regressions return.
Maya B: Final step: set rope.long_context_prefetch FF to 0% globally (rollback).
Leo P: ```curl -X POST https://ff.redwood.internal/toggle -d 'flag=rope.long_context_prefetch&state=off&target=global' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN'```
ops-runbot: Global FF rollback confirmed.
Maya B: All mitigations applied. Observability notes: continuous-batch throughput normalized, KV cache growth stabilized, P99 latency back to baseline.
Ingrid L: I'm taking the on-call handoff in 15m. Leaving these notes in the handoff doc: actions taken, commands used, affected customers, follow-ups.
Maya B: Thanks team. Postmortem action items we should track: 1) add pre-deploy e2e tests for long-context prefetch + continuous batching interactions; 2) add alert for prefetch queue depth growth (auto-mitigation suggested); 3) revert canary rollout gating to require perf-sim tests; 4) add customer impact ticket crosslink.
Sanjay K: I'll open the incident ticket and assign action items.
Maya B: Closing pager. If anything reappears @ingrid please escalate. :white_check_mark:
